guard: the $SYS repair advice instructs exactly when the guard would permit the command it names
why: The delivery daemon told an operator whose observer cred was missing to run `cotal down` then
`cotal up --rotate-sys`. On a root hosting several spaces both verbs are broker-wide and
assertSingleSpaceBroker turns them away - advice that cannot succeed, reached on a real root.
The fix ASKS THE GUARD rather than counting tenants, so the two can never disagree; the corrupt
inventory root is what separates the two, because its readable tenant count is one and only the
guard (which fails closed on unreadable records) refuses. The property is a biconditional, so
the single-tenant arm has to stay instructive: a fix that simply stops naming commands is also
wrong, and mutation 4 is the arm that says so.

mutations.name: the guard's refusal is swallowed, restoring the advice that cannot succeed
mutations.expectRed: the two root: the guard REFUSES and the advice does not instruct
mutations.cell: a multi-tenant root is not handed a command that its own guard refuses

mutations.name: the fail-closed corrupt-inventory refusal is read as permission, as a tenant COUNT would
mutations.replace:
const why = (e as Error).message;
    return why.includes("not fully readable") ? undefined : why;
mutations.expectRed: the corrupt root: the guard REFUSES and the advice does not instruct
mutations.cell: the advice consults the guard itself, not a re-derived tenant count that reads "one" here

mutations.name: the advice paraphrases the refusal instead of quoting it
mutations.find: `${refusal}. There is no other command that mints ${named}: the $SYS signing seed is discarded at provisioning, ` +
mutations.replace: `this root hosts more than one space, so the rotation would refuse. There is no other command that mints ${named}: the $SYS signing seed is discarded at provisioning, ` +
mutations.expectRed: the advice quotes the guard's reasoning verbatim, so the two can never disagree
mutations.cell: the operator reads the guard's own words, so a future refusal reason cannot go unreported

mutations.name: the healthy root stops naming its command too, making the property one-sided
mutations.find: if (refusal === undefined) return "re-mint it with `cotal down` then `cotal up --rotate-sys`";
mutations.replace: if (refusal === undefined) return "re-mint the $SYS pair at the next system-account rotation";
mutations.expectRed: the solo root: the guard PERMITS and the advice instructs
mutations.cell: the single-tenant root keeps its real command - silence everywhere is not the fix
